cultural.vision_reason: This is a traditional beaded, embroidered scroll-patterned collar with pendant beadwork, a type of decorated fish-skin/cloth collar garment made by Amur River peoples including the Nanai; the indigo cloth with scroll embroidery and beaded fringe is consistent with Nanai (or closely related Amur group) costume traditions. The museum record itself attributes production to "Nan[ai]".

physical.title: collar
physical.summary: A man's (?) collar; round neckline, splaying outwards in an arc.  Ground made of dark blue (indigo dyed?) tabby linen (?) cloth.  Finely decorated with embroidered scroll patterning in buttonhole stitch (?), surrounded by isolated scroll motifs worked in chain stitch embroidery.  Stitched to hemline are cream, light and dark blue glass (?) beads of different sizes, threaded in a diamond pattern.  Suspended below beadwork are pendants made of semi-precious stones and pearl-like beads.  Collar piped and lined with natural cream tabby linen cloth.
